title: Tuesday briefing: Katie Hobbs projected to defeat Kari Lake; Trump’s big announcement; Charlottesville shooting; and more
blurb: Catch up in minutes with these 7 stories.

omniture.title: The 7 things you need to know for Tuesday, November 15 - The Washington Post

items.content: Tuesday briefing: Katie Hobbs projected to defeat Kari Lake; Trump’s big announcement; Charlottesville shooting; and more
By Jamie Ross and John Taylor

authors.name: Jamie Ross
authors.bio: Jamie Ross is a writer for The 7, The Washington Post’s morning briefing, which is available each weekday from 7 a.m. to 10 a.m. Eastern time on mobile, desktop and inboxes.
authors.expertise: Newsletter writer focusing on U.S. and world news

authors.name: John Taylor
authors.bio: John Taylor edits The 7, The Washington Post’s morning briefing, which is available each weekday from 7 a.m. to 10 a.m. Eastern time on mobile, desktop and in a newsletter.

items.content: The close race for Arizona governor was called last night.

content: The outcome: Katie Hobbs, a Democrat and Arizona’s secretary of state, was projected to defeat Kari Lake, a Republican and election denier backed by Donald Trump.
Why it matters: Lake wanted to upend the voting system in the key swing state, which could have had big implications for the 2024 election.
What else to know: Republicans are on the cusp of winning control of the House after several close races were settled in three states.

items.content: Trump is expected to launch his 2024 presidential campaign tonight.

content: The event: The former president has promised to make a “big announcement” at his private Mar-a-Lago Club in Florida.
What we know: Trump wants to re-create the underdog vibe of his successful 2016 campaign, and he’ll face many challenges — from fellow Republicans and also multiple investigations.
In other news: Federal agents suspect Trump allegedly took classified documents from the White House as trophies and mementos, The Post has learned.

items.content: We learned more about the deadly shooting at the University of Virginia.

content: The latest: A 22-year-old student was charged yesterday after allegedly opening fire on a bus full of students Sunday in Charlottesville, leaving three people dead and two injured.
The victims: Three people killed — Lavel Davis Jr., D’Sean Perry and Devin Chandler — and at least one of the wounded were U-Va. football players, authorities said.

items.content: Amazon is preparing to carry out massive layoffs.

content: The details: Roughly 10,000 jobs will be cut as soon as this week, which would be the biggest round of layoffs in the company’s history. (Founder Jeff Bezos owns The Post.)
The bigger picture: Amazon will be just the latest tech giant to shrink its workforce, with announcements of steep cuts from Facebook, Twitter, Lyft, Salesforce and others.

items.content: Covid, flu and RSV are keeping kids out of school and parents out of work.

content: What’s happening? This new round of viral infections is colliding with staffing shortages at schools and day cares to create unprecedented challenges for parents and teachers.
The numbers: A record 100,000 Americans missed work last month because of child-care problems, and there are signs that it’s starting to impact the economy.

items.content: Wells are running dry in California at a record pace.

content: Why? The climate is getting hotter and drier. This was the third consecutive year of severe drought, and the state has already tallied 1,351 dry wells in 2022.
What this means: Entire communities are relying on bottled water deliveries to survive.

items.content: Your eating habits could make a big difference to your quality of sleep.

content: How we know: Recent research suggests that steps like cutting out ultra-processed foods can reduce symptoms of sleep apnea, one of the most common causes of bad sleep.
Why it matters: Sleep apnea can raise your blood pressure and increase your risk of developing diabetes and heart disease.

items.content: And now … some tips for your home: How to build a lush plant collection on a budget, and a fix for fading on wood paneling and floors.
Want to catch up quickly with “The 7” every morning? Download The Post’s app and turn on alert notifications for The 7 or sign up for the newsletter.
